paragraphs.source_en: The extinction of the Babenberg family ruling Austria since 976 opened a long dispute between the Bohemian Premyslid family and the Habsburgs, who eventually emerged as dukes of Austria in 1273. 1250–​68 The Staufer collapse. Although named as Frederick II’s successor, Conrad I V had not been crowned and quickly lost ground. The pope used his claims to feudal jurisdiction over Sicily-Naples to reassign this kingdom to Charles of Anjou, brother of the French king. The Anjou line lost Sicily to Aragon in 1282, but retained Naples until 1442. Charles’s execution of Conrad’s son Conradin (1268) definitively ended Staufer attempts to recover their Italian possessions. ‘L i t t l e K i ngs’, 1250 –​1 347 1250–​73 The so‑called Interregnum as rule of the Empire remained contested between several relatively weak monarchs.
